_comment: Single source of truth for awesome-laya. Star counts verified live across the 19001 HK proxy on 2026-10-11. One row per real, public, independently-usable repository in the Laya decision-model ecosystem.

model.name: Laya
model.what: A non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine. Instead of generating text, it returns a typed decision — choice, score, or yes/no — over any input in a single forward pass, in 100+ languages.

layers.description: The model itself. Non-autoregressive System 1 decision engine — typed choice / score / yes-no over any text in a single forward pass, 100+ languages.

items.name: laya
items.what: The reference implementation. One forward pass returns a typed decision (choice, score, or yes/no) instead of generated text, plus a router that picks the right checkpoint per request.

layers.description: Run Laya on your stack — no Python service required. Ports and native runtimes across 10 languages and accelerators.

items.name: laya-mlx
items.what: Native MLX runtime. 7–14 ms short decisions on an M3 Max, with no text generation, no PyTorch, and no cloud API.

items.name: laya-coreml
items.what: Runs typed decisions on Core ML and the Neural Engine. ~5 ms short decisions on M3 Max, with reproducible speed and energy benchmarks.

items.name: laya.cpp
items.what: C++ inference for Laya typed decisions, with CUDA, Vulkan, Core ML, and CPU backends.

items.name: laya
items.what: Run the open-source Jev-compatible Laya model from Node.js and TypeScript via ONNX Runtime.

items.name: laya-php
items.what: Classify text in PHP without an LLM bill — typed decisions in 100+ languages, self-hosted. Laravel-ready.

items.name: lev
items.what: A Jolt (Clojure on the JVM) implementation of the Laya non-autoregressive decision engine.

items.name: Laya4j
items.what: Pure Java 17+ SDK that ports the Laya framework into a production-grade inference library, running fully on the Apache-2.0 checkpoints via ONNX Runtime and HuggingFace Hub.

items.name: laya-go
items.what: Go server plus agent CLI/MCP replacing JEV with open horizontal System 1 decision models (non-autoregressive structured prediction).

items.name: laya-Ascend
items.what: Runs Laya checkpoints on Huawei Ascend NPUs.

items.name: laya-vision
items.what: Image inputs for Laya — calibrated, non-generative typed decisions over images + text (SmolVLM-256M backbone).

layers.description: Stand up a local decision API — the 'Ollama for decision models' layer. Pull, serve, and call typed decisions behind a familiar HTTP interface.

items.name: ollaya
items.what: Run open decision models locally: pull and serve Laya, decider, NLI, and GLiClass behind a TypeSafe-compatible API. 'Ollama for decision models.'

items.name: laya-server
items.what: A self-hosted API and web interface for Laya's structured decision models, compatible with the TypeSafe Jev API format.

items.name: arbiter
items.what: Serve typed-decision (System 1) models — Laya or your own — on NVIDIA GPUs or Apple Silicon, with a Jev-compatible API and coding-agent integrations.

layers.description: Wire Laya into an agent as a fast, cheap judgment layer — MCP servers, frameworks, and platform bindings.

items.name: system-one-connector
items.what: System One MCP connector to evaluate anything fast and cheap — gives your AI agent direct access to Jev, D1, CLM, and Laya.

items.name: FluidUse
items.what: Local computer use on Apple silicon: on-device typed decisions with Laya and form filling with CUA-S1-FORMS, driven through the macOS Accessibility API.

items.name: system1-agents
items.what: System 1 decision models (Jev, Laya, Cua-S1) as the brain for agents: browser use, computer use, games, and robotics.

items.name: omp-laya-judge
items.what: Local Laya System-1 judge MCP server and skill for oh-my-pi: typed decisions in milliseconds, zero LLM tokens.

items.name: home-assistant-laya
items.what: A Home Assistant conversation agent backed by Laya, the multilingual non-autoregressive System 1 decision model.

layers.description: Real products and runnable demos that show Laya replacing an LLM call for a specific job.

items.name: keel
items.what: A local-first macOS coding workspace that uses local Laya and optional Jev decision selection.

items.name: laya-ultrafast
items.what: The ultrafast web-agent loop, rebuilt on Laya instead of a hosted model.

items.name: WechatVibe
items.what: 微信聊天分析工具：本地 Laya ＋ API 模型，提供意图识别、情绪感知、人物画像、群聊画像、好感度与 MBTI 推测。
items.key_capabilities: 意图识别 · 情绪感知 · 人物画像

items.name: laya-playground
items.what: A website, two games, a benchmark, and an agent skill for Laya — all running on your machine.

items.name: laya-vs-jev
items.what: Laya vs Jev: local MLX and hosted AI decisions playing T-Rex side by side, with live metrics and replay recording.

layers.description: The judgment layer around the model — intent contracts, routers, evals, and the sibling decision engines that share Laya's API.

items.name: Intent-Router
items.what: Intent compiler for AI agents — converges vague requests into typed IntentSpec contracts (probe, ask, or halt before routing). The input layer for routers and typed-decision models like Jev and Laya.

items.name: laya_router
items.what: Model routing as a System 1 job: a 421M local decision engine (Laya) vs a GPT-5-nano reasoning router — same accuracy, 35x faster, free.

items.name: jevals
items.what: Agent evals and guardrails as Jev-shaped decisions: one request per trace, a fraction of a cent, fast enough for the agent loop. Runs locally with Kev or Laya.

items.name: openJev-verdict-2.0
items.what: A calibrated 151M non-autoregressive decision engine benchmarked against TypeSafe Jev and Laya (77.10% acc, 0.0636 Brier, 0.0144 ECE).

items.name: OpenJev
items.what: Self-evolving cognitive decision engine and TypeSafe Jev alternative — a System 2→1 decision flywheel with 100% option-order invariance and a typed probabilistic API for open LLMs, Laya, and commercial Jev.
